title: Betfred ends sponsorship of all British Classics after UK tax increases
article_text:
UK gambling firm Betfred has announced it has ended its sponsorship of horseracing’s British Classics, five of the oldest and most important English races, as it continues its exit from sport commitments on the back of rising taxes.

Betfred said it was left with “no choice” but to walk away from its partnerships with Jockey Club and Arena Racing Company following the latest tax increase announced in the UK Government's latest budget.

The latest budget increased MGD from 20% to 25%, a rise the company said could put 1,420 jobs at risk.

Ahead of the budget announcement, Betfred’s co-founder and chairman Fred Done suggested the company would back out of its deal covering the 1000 and 2000 Guineas at Newmarket, the Derby and Oaks at Epsom, and the St Leger at Doncaster if UK Chancellor John Healey increased machine games duty (MGD).

The termination comes three years after Betfred took over sponsorship of the Derby, Oaks, and St Leger in 2023 and secured Newmarket’s 2,000 Guineas and 1,000 Guineas from 2025.

A Betfred spokesperson said: “Following successive tax rises for the betting industry – and in particular the increase to machine games duty at the most recent Budget – it is with great sadness that we have taken the difficult decision not to proceed with a three-year renewal of our sponsorship of the British Classics.

“It is not a decision we wanted to make, but the cumulative cost of government policy has left us with no choice.”

The news comes shortly after Betfred announced it would end its long-standing title sponsorship of British rugby league’s Super League this year.

Betfred has put its name to the 14-team Super League since 2017 but said it will not renew its contract when it ends at the conclusion of the 2026 season.

The most recent deal between the pair was struck in October 2023 and was valued at more than £3 million ($4 million) per year at the time, according to GlobalData Sport.

At the time, Done also cited the UK government's most recent budget and the ensuing combination of tax rises and wage inflation that has forced the company to reevaluate its spending.

Last year, it also let its deal covering golf's British Masters expire, with Swedish robotic lawnmowing specialist Husqvarna then taking its place in February.

Betfred, meanwhile, is also a sponsor of top-tier darts action through 2030, through a deal with the Professional Darts Corporation.

Amy Starkey, who runs Epsom as managing director of the Jockey Club’s London Hub, said: “While we are naturally disappointed that Betfred have taken the decision not to renew their sponsorship of the Derby and the Guineas Festival at Newmarket, we understand their reasons for doing so and know this was not an easy decision for them.

“We are currently in conversations with a number of interested prospective partners that share our ambitions for the future of both events and look forward to sharing more details in due course.”

title: Sky Sports partners with Sir Gareth Southgate’s 1071 Media
article_text:
Sky Sports and 1071 Media, the production company founded by former England manager Sir Gareth Southgate and Jimmy Worrall, will make and distribute three long-form football shows for social and digital platforms. Sky Media will handle commercial sales for all three.

The Football Dugout is a new weekly podcast and YouTube show presented by Sky Sports’ Mark Chapman and former England defender Conor Coady, who is now coaching with England U21s. Guests will include managers, players, coaches and sporting directors. The show is recorded in The Pod, a mobile studio that travels to guests, and will launch on its own YouTube channel and on the main audio platforms.

The Football Boardcast is a renamed version of 1071 Media’s existing show The Football Boardroom, which launched earlier this year. It is hosted by former Liverpool, Chelsea and Aston Villa executive Christian Purslow and journalist Henry Winter, and covers money, power and politics in football. It stays on its existing YouTube and audio channels.

The Football Data Room is a new data-led analysis show on the Sky Sports Premier League YouTube channel. It is presented by Sky Sports Saturday Social host Joe Thomlinson with analysts “Statman Dave” and Jamie Osman, formerly of West Ham United and Ipswich Town. Up to three 20-minute episodes will be released each week, covering match reviews, previews and opinion.

The shows add to Sky Sports’ social output. The broadcaster passed one billion engagements across its social platforms earlier this year and now has more than 130 million aggregated subscribers across those channels. It is showing more than 1,500 live games this season across the Premier League, EFL, SPFL and WSL, and from 2027/28 will also show every UEFA Europa League and UEFA Conference League match.

Jonathan Licht, CEO of Sky Sports UK & Ireland, said, “We have years of expertise, an unmatched passion for sport and huge reach. Combining that with 1071 Media’s creativity and insight, we can create compelling new football content and take it to fans wherever and however they choose to engage with the game.”

Sir Gareth Southgate, Co-Founder of 1071 Media, said, “With the launch of three football shows covering the boardroom, the boot room and the data room, we hope fans gain greater insight into the business, the tactics, and the analysis to explain how the game really works. We couldn’t ask for a better partner than Sky Sports, who have set the standard in broadcasting for decades.”

title: McLaren Racing signs multi-year Formula 1 partnership with NTT
article_text:
Japanese technology group NTT will join the McLaren Mastercard Formula 1 Team from the 2027 season, on a multi-year agreement focused on artificial intelligence security.

NTT will help the team with its aim of becoming the most AI-fluent team on the grid, with AI security governance central to the work. Its role includes supporting the framework McLaren uses to manage security risks arising from its use of AI, and helping the team adopt the technology responsibly. NTT will also run a global engagement programme for clients and fans, using the partnership to show how its technology supports McLaren on and off the track.

The work will be delivered with the team at the McLaren Technology Centre in Woking, the base of a British team that won back-to-back Constructors’ Championships in 2024 and 2025 and took the 2025 Drivers’ title with Lando Norris. In 2025, McLaren won its first Drivers’ title since 2008. This season, under F1’s new technical regulations, the team is third in the Constructors’ standings behind Mercedes and Ferrari.

The agreement builds on a relationship that dates back to the McLaren-Honda era. NTT Communications, now NTT DOCOMO BUSINESS, provided network, cloud and data connectivity to the Woking team across sites including the UK. NTT DATA later partnered the Arrow McLaren IndyCar Team, and NTT has been title sponsor of the NTT INDYCAR SERIES since 2019.

NTT is the latest in a run of technology and AI companies to join or extend with McLaren. Groq joined in 2025 to provide AI inference, Google extended its partnership to put its Gemini AI model at the centre of the team’s operations, Cisco renewed in July, and Intel returned to Formula 1 with McLaren this year. Okta, Rubrik and Dell Technologies are also partners of the team.

Zak Brown, CEO of McLaren Racing, said, “AI has enormous potential across our sport and our business, and NTT’s expertise will support us in adopting new technologies in a responsible and secure way.”

Akira Shimada, President and CEO of NTT, said, “Formula 1 is a global stage where the world’s brightest minds come together to continuously push the limits of what is possible. Since 2019, NTT has contributed to the growth of motorsport through its title sponsorship of the NTT INDYCAR SERIES. This new partnership builds on that experience, and together with McLaren Racing, we will further accelerate NTT’s global business.”

title: Wales opt for centre power pair against Japan
article_text:
Wales head coach Steve Tandy has opted for power in his centre partnership by bringing in Max Llewellyn alongside Eddie James for the Nations Championship opener against Japan on Saturday (16:40 GMT).

Llewellyn, 6ft 6in (1.96m) and 16st 12lbs (107kg) and James, 6ft 4in (1.90m) and 16st 3lbs (103kg), will form one of Wales' biggest midfield combinations.

Tandy has abandoned his policy of selecting a more recognised ball-player at inside centre with Llewellyn named in the 12 jersey.

Fly-half Sam Costelow is preferred to Dan Edwards, while wings Josh Adams and Louis Rees-Zammit and full-back Blair Murray form the back three.

Props Nicky Smith and Archie Griffin start alongside captain Dewi Lake, while Dafydd Jenkins has shaken off a knee injury to resume his Six Nations partnership with Ben Carter. Alex Mann, Jac Morgan and Aaron Wainwright form the back row.

Tandy has made seven personnel changes from the side that lost 43-0 against South Africa in July.

Nine of the 15 starters against Japan, including six of the eight forwards, and 12 of the 23-strong squad, play club rugby in England.

There are three Scarlets players, two from Cardiff, one Dragon and no Ospreys, although half-backs Edwards and Reuben Morgan-Williams have been named as replacements.

"There's lots of competition for positions within the squad, which is where we want to be," said Tandy.

This will be Tandy's sixth different centre partnership in his 13th international in charge, with Joe Hawkins or Ben Thomas having being given the number 12 jersey in the previous 12 internationals.

Thomas and Llewellyn were the Wales duo that started against South Africa in July.

Thomas is missing because of a calf injury while Hawkins has been left out of the 23-strong squad for the autumn games.

Llewellyn played most of his early senior rugby for Cardiff at inside centre before leaving for Gloucester, where he has played more at outside centre alongside England midfield-man Seb Atkinson at Kingsholm.

Before the start of the season, Llewellyn told BBC Sport Wales inside centre was his preferred position.

He has only worn the number 12 shirt for Gloucester on one occasion this season, and started just once at inside centre for Wales in a World Cup warm-up game against England in August 2023.

James has also came though the Scarlets as a more natural 12 but Tandy says he sees the Wales future of the 24-year-old from Carmarthen at 13.

"We're excited to see the pairing," said Tandy.

"We've had a couple of training sessions together, and it's been really good to watch.

"There's strong competition, and you can't overlook Max's form since returning.

"He also had a run at number 12 against Bath, His defensive performances have been excellent, but he can also play with the ball.

"He's played at inside centre regularly for Cardiff, so we're confident he can deliver what we're looking for.

"So we're looking forward to seeing what the partnership can produce."

Wales started the Nations Championship campaign in July with a victory against Fiji before defeats against Argentina and South Africa.

After resuming the campaign against Japan, Wales will host New Zealand and Australia in successive Saturdays before travelling to the Allianz Stadium in Twickenham on the final weekend of November to face yet unknown opposition in the play-off games.

"We're excited to be to back at home," said Tandy.

"We want to go out there on Saturday, put our mark on the match and start the next phase in our Nations Championship campaign strongly."

Wales and Japan both currently lie fifth in their respective hemisphere tables.

In July, Japan beat Italy but lost to Ireland and France in the opening three games of the tournament.

Wales: Murray; Rees-Zammit, James, Llewellyn, Adams; Costelow, Tomos Williams; Smith, Lake (capt), Griffin, Jenkins, Carter, Mann, Morgan, Wainwright.

Replacements: Elias, Carre, Francis, Teddy Williams, Botham, Morgan-Williams, D Edwards, Hennessey.

title: England must improve discipline says RFU chief Bill Sweeney
article_text:
England must improve their discipline given they are the second-best side in the world when they have 15 players on the pitch, says Rugby Football Union chief executive Bill Sweeney.

During a miserable Six Nations campaign, England received eight yellow cards and one red across five matches, meaning they played 118 minutes - almost a game and a half of rugby - at less than a full complement.

They finished the 45-21 defeat by South Africa in July with 13 men after yellow cards for Tommy Freeman and Guy Pepper, while four second-half sin-binnings contributed to Argentina coming close to a successful fightback a fortnight later.

"It has been a big internal discussion," said Sweeney, who claims analysis also shows England slip to eighth or ninth best in the world when they are down to 14 players.

"[Head coach] Steve [Borthwick]'s very conscious of that and he's working really hard with the players to improve that aspect.

"You need all your players on the pitch for as long as possible. That's something we need to address."

England face Australia on Sunday in the first match of their November campaign.

Borthwick's side comfortably won last autumn's meeting between the two teams, but the Wallabies' shock 42-37 victory in 2024 is a recent reminder of their quality.

After matches against Japan (14 November) and New Zealand (21 November), England will play another southern hemisphere opponent in the first Nations Championship finals weekend at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham.

The new biennial event, introduced to bring a clearer narrative to the Test calendar outside of Rugby World Cup and British and Irish Lions tour years, culminates in six play-off matches over three days.

The teams at the top of the northern and southern hemisphere standings will play off for the Nations Championship title, while all matches count towards a Ryder Cup-style Hemisphere Shield trophy.

Sweeney admitted ticket sales for Friday's fixtures - which will see the sixth-placed and third-placed teams in their respective standings face off at 16:40 and 20:10 GMT respectively - had been "challenging" as the new tournament attempts to fill an 82,000-seater venue.

The upper tier of Allianz Stadium has yet to be opened, with plenty of seats still available in the lower section.

The identity of the teams involved in Friday's play-offs will only be finalised after the previous weekend's action.

With three of six rounds played, the current standings would pit Italy against Fiji in the day's first game, and England against Australia in its headline fixture.

"It's uncharted waters," Sweeney told BBC Sport of the finals weekend.

"Saturday and Sunday ticket sales are going well - Friday's a challenge at the moment.

"We're waiting to see how things go after this weekend when things start to firm up a bit and you'll get a better idea of where the league rankings are.

"A lot of fans still don't fully understand what it is and we've done a fair bit of education, but maybe not enough.

"Friday does remain a challenge, but we're confident that we'll see an uptick in ticket sales."

The organisers of the tournament, which is a joint venture between the Six Nations and Rugby Championship organisers Sanzaar, will hope to avoid a backdrop of empty seats for the start of their new showpiece.

They have already had to negotiate a change of plan for the second edition of the Nations Championship.

A provisional schedule had been mapped out with Qatar hosting a lucrative finals weekend in 2028, before the event was transplanted to the USA in 2030 to drive interest in the sport in the country which hosts the 2031 Rugby World Cup.

However, the US-Israel war with Iran, and the broader instability that has caused in the Middle East, has brought alternative arrangements to the fore - with Spain, keen to prove itself having bid for the 2035 Rugby World Cup, a possible host for 2028.

"There's a conversation between wanting the most commercial return or wanting to develop the tournament and have greater accessibility for the fans," said Sweeney.

"It could be that a return to London is the best thing in the interest of the competition. It could be that you go to France and host it there.

"It could be you go to Spain or it could be Middle Eastern interest is still there and they'd want to host it somewhere else."

Six Nations and Sanzaar decided at a recent meeting in Sydney to set up a dedicated team to focus full-time on running the Nations Championship and accelerate the event's development.

title: Q&A: DP World Tour CEO Guy Kinnings bullish on growth amid LIV Golf uncertainty
article_text:
DP World Tour CEO Guy Kinnings has “delivered a bullish but, at the same time, realistic update on the circuit,” describing the current uncertainty surrounding LIV Golf as a “chance for all of golf to ‘reset,’” according to a Q&A by Martin Dempster of THE SCOTSMAN. Kinnings spoke openly about several key aspects of the tour, “from speculation about the current health of the circuit to the wellbeing of its members and its plans for membership and invites for next season.” Questions and answers have been edited for clarity and brevity.

Q: What are your thoughts on the DP World Tour in the current landscape?

Kinnings: “Our financial structure, like any global business, is complicated. … But the reality shows that there is some real strength, some stuff which makes me bullish about now and what we’re going to do going forward. We have strong cash reserves, but the thing that’s most notable for me is our record sponsorship levels. … We’re over 100 per cent up from 2019 to 2025 with over a billion dollars currently contracted across the Tour. … And it’s not just the sponsorship. You’ve got TV viewership up seven per cent this year alongside consumer levels in terms of ticketing and merch and hospitality up 30 per cent year on year. So people are engaged.”

Q: People seem to be doubting that the Strategic Alliance with the PGA Tour would continue in a non-LIV era. Do you worry about that scenario unfolding?

Kinnings: “The Strategic Alliance has worked really well for both parties. The PGA Tour has benefited having us as partners with everything they’ve had to deal with and we have unquestionably benefitted from their financial support. … We’re working on it right now. We haven’t resolved everything and there are things yet to be worked out. … We both want to get it done. I have every confidence we will.”

Q: Are DP World Tour members right to be irked about LIV players talking about returning to the tour?

Kinnings: “I listen to what players say and I understand the sensitivity. It’s got to be as fair as it can be and as merit based as it can be, but there is probably no perfect solution. … We’ve got to protect that special culture that we have on the Tour. … But we also have to protect the Tour against an entity who spent, so we are told, over $7 billion, with one of their aims being to ‘destroy the DP World Tour.’ … Clearly when you are faced with statements like that, and then people then ask why we are doing what we are doing with our membership and invite policy for 2027, then I think the answer becomes pretty obvious” (THE SCOTSMAN, 11/3).

title: Money-making Nations Championship project carries a cost for fans and players
article_text:
It was a loose kick, tumbling aimlessly end over end into the All Blacks’ half. Their wing Billy Wallace gathered it and sprinted into midfield, through a gap and on into the Welsh half, only their full-back ahead of him now, and with his teammate Bob Deans in the corner of his eye, coming on the inside calling for the ball. Wallace gave the pass and Deans was away, making straight for the posts, tackled at the last moment by Rhys Gabe, and the two of them went sliding for the try‑line together. The ball finished in the tips of Deans’s fingers, at the end of his outstretched arm.

Over the line? On the line? Inches away from the line?

No one knows. The referee John Dewar Dallas insisted that Deans never made it. The match finished 3-0 to Wales: the All Blacks’ solitary defeat in 35 games on their 1905 autumn tour of Europe. Lloyd Jones wrote a great novel about that tour, Carl Nixon turned it into a successful play, Nigel Wray paid £180,000 for the jersey the All Blacks captain Dave Gallaher wore on the day. You can still buy a DVD of a “dramatic reconstruction” of the match, and a century later two Kiwi journalists published a book offering what they considered new, definitive proof about what happened.

Some 121 years later, if you ever want to start an argument, you can walk into the backroom of any Welsh rugby pub and tell the first old boy at the bar that of course Deans scored. Or walk into any Kiwi rugby club bar and say you’re sure he never did.

There are no autumn tours this year. Instead we have the conclusion of the new Nations Championship, starting in Dublin when Ireland play Argentina on Friday night. It’s a tournament designed to provide a context that was apparently lacking in that legendary match between Wales and New Zealand.

Over the next three weekends France, Ireland and Italy all have matches against Argentina, Fiji and South Africa. England, Scotland and Wales play Australia, Japan, and New Zealand, and at the end there are six games in three days across a long weekend at Twickenham, sixth place in the northern group against sixth in the southern, and so on, all the way until the top two teams play each other at tea-time on Sunday. The “Hemisphere Shield” will be awarded to whoever comes out top in what is being described as a “Ryder Cup style” competition.

It took the sport the best part of a decade to cobble this competition together. World Rugby first suggested it in 2018, but it took the massive debts left by the Covid pandemic to concentrate minds and get the Six Nations, Sanzaar and all their respective private investors to collaborate on making it happen. After all that time they have ended up with a competition that brings to mind the old line about a camel being a horse designed by committee. God knows the game needs the money, but you have to ask if the organisers needed to give away so much of what people love about the sport to get it.

The Nations Championship has been designed with commercial returns in mind. It is a tournament that seems to have been made almost entirely made for TV. Which is why there are so many compromises. The integrity of the competition wasn’t high on the priorities list, which is why Fiji played their “home” games against Wales in Cardiff, England in Liverpool, and Scotland at Murrayfield in the summer, and Japan were made to stage their own match against Ireland in Australia, to save their opponents an extra trip after a fixture against the Wallabies. Player welfare doesn’t seem to have played much of a part in anyone’s thinking either, so England found themselves flying 25,000 miles to play three fixtures in three weeks on three different continents.

Nor did spectator experience: the whole thing seems to have been designed to deter travelling fans, and risk gate revenue, since the organisers now have to find a way to sell half a million tickets for six fixtures where it won’t be clear who is playing when until six days before kick-off, something they’ve done by offering “support your team” tickets that guarantee you a seat at a match you actually want to watch, regardless of when it’s played. It’s a small mercy that the deal with Qatar has just fallen through so at least we’ve been spared the second edition being staged in the Gulf.

It will work. We’ll all watch. If you love rugby the chances are you were going to tune in for these games anyway. France v South Africa in Paris on a Friday night, England v Australia at Twickenham on a cold autumn afternoon, Scotland v New Zealand on a Saturday at Murrayfield: the truth is these matches don’t need selling, their significance has nothing to do with a competition structure that has been cooked up in the commercial department. It’s enough to make you wonder if the people who sell the sport even really understand why people buy it in the first place.

title: Lady Cranes chase SVNS 3 ticket
Scotland team named for All Blacks with Russell to bring up Test century
article_text:
Scotland head coach Gregor Townsend has picked 10 Glasgow Warriors in the starting line-up to face the All Blacks at Murrayfield on Saturday.

There is a surprise starting place for Rory Sutherland ahead of Pierre Schoeman at loosehead prop, with the Edinburgh man having to make do with a place on the bench.

Sutherland, a British & Irish Lions tourist in 2021 who earned his 50th cap during the summer tour, has been included just once for Glasgow this season, partly due to a calf injury.

Ewan Ashman is the only player from the capital club included in the starting XV despite their good start to the new season.

Gregor Brown partners Scott Cummings in the second row, while Matt Fagerson is fit to start in the back-row alongside current Glasgow colleague Rory Darge and former Warrior Jack Dempsey.

Behind the scrum, Kyle Rowe has been preferred to British & Irish Lion Blair Kinghorn at fullback, while Huw Jones gets the nod over Rory Hutchinson and Stafford McDowall to partner captain Sione Tuipulotu in the midfield.

Finn Russell will win his 100th international cap as he makes his 96th appearance for Scotland, adding to the four Tests he's played for the Lions.

There is no place in the squad for record try-scorer Darcy Graham or his long-time wing colleague Duhan van der Merwe.

title: 'A tough few days' - Dave Rennie on All Blacks' grief after Cadwallader's death
article_text:
Dave Rennie admits the sudden passing of security chief Logan Cadwallader has "rocked" the All Blacks squad.

Cadwallader, who was with the All Blacks for 10 years, passed away following a medical incident at the team hotel on Sunday night.

"It's been a tough few days," said a visibly emotional Rennie.

The former Glasgow Warriors coach added: "He was such a good man, he meant a hell of a lot to the team, so there's been a big emotional toll.

"We've had his brother here and his best mate, so it's been a chance to get together and share stories, so it's helped. But it has really rocked the squad.

"Our thoughts, obviously, with Nannette and the kids, and Trey is on his way over here, which will be pretty special."

Gregor Townsend also paid tribute to the long-serving All Blacks head of security.

"I can only imagine how tough that would be for everybody in the group, for those that knew Logan well.

“It must have been a really tough time, and it brings the group closer together, undoubtedly, when you're going through shared pain."

Townsend does not, though, expect the trauma of the week to influence the All Blacks' performance.

"I'm sure that it won't really change much about how they play. The All Blacks have a consistent mindset and performance level that we're expecting the weekend.

“They know if they don't perform well, the criticism comes hard in their country. Rugby is so big for them, so we're expecting one of their best performances against us."

Scottish Rugby are planning a tribute to Cadwallader before Saturday's game, with details being finalised in conjunction with the family and the All Blacks.

title: Newport to host men's professional tennis in 2027
article_text:
Newport Tennis Centre will host Wales' highest level men's tournament next year.

Taking place from 24-31 January, the M25 event will attract international players ranked approximately 200-400 in the world.

It is a level all of Wales' top players have competed at, so James Story, Finn Murrgett and Viktor Frydrych could all be involved.

The singles and doubles champions will secure $25,000 (£18,500) in prize money, plus ranking points towards competing on the professional tour.

The announcement follows the success of the ladies' W100 tournament which will return to Wrexham for a third year in October 2027.

Mark Lewis, Tennis Wales' competition and events manager, said: "We are delighted to bring the Lexus British Pro Series Newport M25 to south Wales.

"Hosting a tournament of this level provides an outstanding opportunity for Welsh players to compete on home soil while inspiring the next generation of players and fans."

title: WTA offers Jodie Burrage support after death threats, online abuse following Chennai defeat
article_text:
The Women’s Tennis Association (WTA) has offered additional support to British player Jodie Burrage after she received death threats and online abuse following her first-round defeat at the Chennai Open in India.

Burrage shared several messages sent to her Instagram account after losing 3-6, 6-3, 7-5 to India’s Vaishnavi Adkar on Tuesday.

“Nice welcome back to tour. I remember why I left,” the 27-year-old wrote alongside the messages.

The match was Burrage’s first WTA Tour singles main-draw appearance in 16 months. Adkar’s victory was the Indian player’s first at WTA level.

The WTA said staff attending the tournament in Chennai were supporting Burrage alongside its player welfare and Threat Matrix teams.

The organization has also offered her access to a private channel for reporting abusive direct messages and a moderation service that conceals offensive public comments before players see them.

The abusive messages have been reported to the relevant social media platforms, while investigations are underway to identify the account holders.

Accounts linked to gambling-related abuse could also be referred to the Bad Actor program, allowing betting operators to take action against users connected to them.

The WTA launched the AI-assisted Threat Matrix system with other tennis organizations in 2023 to identify and investigate threats directed at players and officials.

"Protecting players and the wider tennis family from online threats and abuse is a key priority for the WTA," the organization told BBC Sport.

The system combines artificial intelligence with human analysis to monitor public posts across Instagram, X, Facebook, TikTok and YouTube. It can also refer serious threats to law enforcement and assist in assessing risks to players’ physical safety.

A WTA report released in July said the program secured the removal of 66% of serious abusive posts and comments identified during 2025.

Thirty-five accounts were escalated to law enforcement, while 89% of accounts responsible for serious abuse in 2024 did not reappear the following year.

Burrage previously spoke about online abuse after her first-round loss at Wimbledon in 2025, saying players often received hostile messages from gamblers blaming them for losing money.

Other players expressed support for Burrage following her latest post, including Germany’s Eva Lys, who publicly called for further action against online abuse.

title: Sportfive extends Borrusia Dortmund marketing tie-up until 2034
article_text:
Borussia Dortmund (BVB), of German soccer’s top-tier Bundesliga, has struck an early extension of its long-standing commercial marketing deal with international sports agency Sportfive, adding another three years to its agreement.

The new deal builds on the pair’s original marketing tie-up in 1999 and their most recent renewal in 2023, which took the contract to June 2031.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

Under the extension, Sportfive will continue to support BVB in acquiring and managing sponsors and partners, developing new commercial opportunities, and marketing hospitality offerings at home ground Signal Iduna Park.

Carsten Cramer, chief executive of BVB, said: “Our partnership with Sportfive has been defined by trust, reliability and an entrepreneurial mindset for many years. Together, we have continuously developed our commercial activities and unlocked significant growth opportunities.

“We are therefore delighted to continue this successful journey until 2034. With Sportfive, we have a partner at our side who understands our ambitions and supports us in further developing Borussia Dortmund both nationally and internationally.”

Looking forward, the agency said in addition to developing existing partnerships, the focus will be on opening new business areas, innovative activation approaches, and BVB’s international positioning.

BVB’s range of commercial partners includes Vodafone (main shirt sponsor), Puma (kit sponsor), Signal Iduna (stadium naming rights) and Evonik (major partner), as well as Coca-Cola, Eurowings, Coinbase, Konami, Melitta, Topps, DeWALT, and ABB, among others.

Hendrik Schiphorst, Managing Director of Sportfive Germany, said: “Borussia Dortmund is one of Europe’s best-known and most distinctive football brands.

“The early extension until 2034 is a strong endorsement of the quality of our partnership and, at the same time, an incentive to continue pursuing our shared growth trajectory. We look forward to further developing BVB’s commercial activities in the years ahead with fresh ideas and great passion.”

The early extension consolidates Sportfive’s client portfolio in German soccer, having secured a partnership with the DFL governing body until 2029 to sell integrated sports packages for the relegation matches in the Bundesliga and second-tier Bundesliga 2, as well as the season-opening Franz Beckenbauer Supercup.

Along with BVB, other German soccer clubs under Sportfive include Stuttgart, Augsburg, Union Berlin, Eintracht Frankfurt, Borussia Monchengladbach, and 1899 Hoffenheim.

Meanwhile, BVB’s women’s team has secured health technology and smart ring company RingConn as a premium partner.

As part of the partnership, some players in the BVB team will receive RingConn Gen 3 smart rings for continued use.

BVB managing director Svenja Schlenker said: “We are pleased to welcome RingConn as a Premium Partner of our women's football team.

“Our players are defined by commitment, individuality and a strong connection to their bodies, and this partnership supports exactly that. Listening to your body and understanding your own rhythm helps everyone perform and feel well, on the pitch and in everyday life.”

title: NHL and Kaufland in tie-up covering pair of German games
article_text:
North American ice hockey's top-tier NHL has entered into a multi-year international commercial deal with German retail chain Kaufland.

Through a tie-up unveiled today, the brand becomes the presenting sponsor for the NHL's upcoming two-game Germany series, now called the NHL Global Series Germany presented by Kaufland. It will then retain this role for the duration of the tie-up.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The Germany games will take place on December 18 and 20 in Dusseldorf, with the Ottawa Senators and Chicago Blackhawks competing in both.

In addition, Kaufland becomes the 32-team league's official grocery retail partner in Germany, Czechia, and Slovakia.

The brand is now set to benefit from in-arena brand presence at the two Dusseldorf games, as well as on digitally-enhanced dasherboards, and on virtual in-ice advertisements during game broadcasts (including during broadcasts of games at Europe-friendly times).

In terms of Kaufland's upcoming activations, meanwhile, the supermarket chain is set to provide both in-store and digital fan experiences, the opportunity to win NHL-themed prizes, and "integration of the NHL brand" into its print and digital marketing efforts.

Jason Jazayeri, group vice president of business development at the NHL, commented: "Kaufland’s extensive reach and deep connection to consumers make them an ideal partner as we continue to grow the NHL’s presence across Europe. Together, we have a tremendous opportunity to bring hockey closer to fans through meaningful engagement at retail, across our Global Series events and in local communities."

This Germany-specific tie-up follows on from the NHL unveiling a major agreement – Europe-wide – with global logistics and delivery giant DHL, late last month.

That deal covers the Germany games, as well as a pair of games taking place in Finland later this month, featuring the Carolina Hurricanes and Seattle Kraken.

Around one-third of the total number of contracted NHL players are European.

Michael Luttgen, a member of the executive board at Kaufland, added: "Ice hockey is not new territory for us: in the Czech Republic and Slovakia, we at Kaufland have already been successfully involved in the sport for years. Together with the NHL, we are now taking this commitment to a new international level."

Elsewhere in sports, Kaufland is also a partner of the International Ski and Snowboard Federation, as well as of the German Ski Association.

In terms of other recent NHL commercial activity, mid-October saw the ice hockey league and holiday booking service Expedia announce a new deal.

title: Huge ambitions and milestone moments as World Rugby Nations Cup returns
article_text:
The inaugural World Rugby Nations Cup resumes this weekend, as the game’s best and most ambitious emerging teams continue their quest for victory. A champion will be crowned from each pool, with the United States and Georgia currently occupying prime positions in their respective groups.

Stay tuned all week as RugbyPass counts down the 50 best women’s rugby players in the world, culminating with the No.1 player reveal this Friday. See who has already made the list...

Chile and Portugal are hot on their heels, however, and other major players are jostling for position and momentum as the countdown to Rugby World Cup 2027 intensifies.

Matches will be staged as far and wide as Lisbon, Angouleme and Hong Kong China this month, creating a colourful backdrop to a tournament worthy of your attention.

After three rounds, USA in pool A and Georgia in pool B reigned supreme, coming out of the opening block of matches in July with three wins and 14 points apiece. The Eagles and the Lelos bagged a bonus point in every game except against Portugal and Samoa, respectively, showing their dominance.

With Luka Matkava and Christopher Hilsenbeck masterfully pulling the strings and the likes of Perry Mayo (what an impact the winger had for the USA), Tornike Jalagonia, Kapeli Pifeleti and Ilia Spanderashvili massively influencing each game, it wasn’t a surprise when USA and Georgia came through the month unscathed.

While most didn’t think the Romanian Stejarii could mount a title challenge, the truth is David Gérard’s side had enough firepower to draw against Uruguay and land a monumental last-play win over Samoa. As the Eastern European country’s set-piece looks to be bolstered and a dynamic running backline which delivered nine of their 15 tries in July developes, it wouldn’t be a shock if Romania collect at least two wins in November.

Portugal are stocked with trailblazing firepower in the form of Rodrigo Marta, who is the Top 14’s second-top try-scorer, Manuel Cardoso Pinto, Nicolás Martins, Cody Lee Thomas, Manuel Vareiro and Tomás Appleton. In July, they went to North America without Marta and Martins, but still defeated Canada and Tonga.

Chile, who will be hosted by the Lobos on Saturday, will have Lucas Berti, Rodrigo Fernández, Matías Garafulic, Martín Singren, and Diego Escobar as their leading superstars. Pablo Lemoine’s side has the gritty ambition to land three historic wins, which should set off alarms in Portugal, Spain and Zimbabwe. In July, the Cóndores delivered two stunning performances against Romania and Hong Kong China, but couldn’t topple Georgia.

Meanwhile, Hong Kong China created one of the most spectacular results of the fledgling tournament, beating World Cup regulars Uruguay for the first time ever. With seconds remaining, Logan Asplin’s side trailed by two points and won a penalty just inside Los Teros’ half. Having successfully landed five out of six kicks up to that point, Paul Altier eyed up the posts one last time before striking the ball cleanly between the uprights, sparking wild celebrations.

This moment was the Nations Cup in microcosm: history made, a record broken, and a moment enshrined in Hong Kong China rugby folklore.

The Nations Cup is about much more than the fixtures themselves. Teams en masse have embraced what the competition has offered them. Portugal captain and icon Tomas Appleton sees wide-ranging benefits of regular, guaranteed and meaningful Test matches for his side.

“The Nations Cup is a great competition for us, as it allows us to develop our core team and game plan, but without losing sight of the competitive side,” he says. “We want to play against the top teams, but the Nations Cup provides us with a platform to play competitive games.

“We now know we are going to play at least six games in November and July, which makes it easier for us to prepare and get fans in the stands. It isn’t a World Cup, but it is not far off, as the environment and landscape have some similarities.”

Having captained Portugal to their maiden Rugby World Cup win in 2023, and co—skippered the Lobos to their first Rugby Europe Championship title in almost three decades earlier this year, Appleton has lofty ambitions.

“We want to win every game. We can’t shy away from being favourites and we will be looking to show how alive and ready the Lobos are!”

Spain will not meet their Iberian neighbours this month, but Los Leones will compete for a chance to reach the top, while earning vital reps to ready themselves for a long-awaited return to the World Cup.

“Having the chance to face and compete with teams on the same stage of development as us, who will also be playing in the next World Cup, undoubtedly benefits our growth,” says captain Jon Zabala.

“The Nations Cup isn’t just about the title. The chance to compete against Tonga and Samoa, two very physical teams, gives us the opportunity to grow other areas of the game, which is key for our future.”

With Spain hosting games in Madrid, Leganés and Málaga, the Section Paloise prop and his teammates are determined to deliver more than a few special memories to their fans.

“We have a lot of expectations for November. Uruguay, Chile, and Samoa are going to be huge spectacles, and we’ll be targeting those three games, for sure. We want to finish on a high and have the chance to celebrate on the podium.”

title: Injury-hit France hand out debut against Fiji
article_text:
Bayonne back-row Esteban Capilla is set to make his France debut on Saturday against Fiji in the Nations Championship in Lyon after being named on the bench by Fabien Galthie.

After Toulouse back-row Anthony Jelonch joined France’s sizeable injury list at the weekend after sustaining a head injury in the latest round of Top 14 action, Galthie has turned to the 23-year-old for France Sevens international as his back-row cover on the bench.

Jelonch is a member of a casualty list that includes Emmanuel Meafou, Thibaud Flament, Matthieu Jalibert and Thomas Ramos. In his absence, Francois Cros will start at No.8, with Cameron Woki and Paul Boudehent on either flank.

There are nevertheless plenty of star names in the team, with captain Antoine Dupont set to reprise his half-back partnership with club-mate Romain Ntamack in blue for the first time since March 2025. A series of injuries for the pair, as well as strategic rests, have prevented the duo from gracing the Test scene together.

Despite losing Meafou and Flament in the engine room, Galthie has stuck with four second-rows in his squad with a 6-2 split on the bench. Montpellier’s Florian Verhaeghe and Lyon’s Mickaël Guillard will start the match, with Charles Ollivon and Tom Staniforth chosen on the bench.

title: WTA takes 'full responsibility' after Pegula 'diva' comment live-streamed
article_text:
The Women's Tennis Association says it takes "full responsibility" for not telling players there were microphones on practice courts after private comments Jessica Pegula made to her coach about fellow player Mirra Andreeva were live-streamed.

The session at Indian Wells, California, was streamed by the WTA before its Tour Finals start on Sunday.

In a private conversation with her coach Mark Knowles, world number five Pegula described Andreeva as "a diva".

The American could also be heard saying the French Open champion "needs to be humbled" and her coach Conchita Martinez encourages her behaviour.

Pegula's agent, Chris McCormack, said she had been "completely unaware" the conversation could be heard by courtside microphones, "let alone live-streamed to the public".

"Naturally it's been an unfortunate situation for everyone involved," McCormack told BBC Sport.

"Jess has since been in direct contact with those involved, which she felt was important to do personally rather than through the media."

YouTube streams of Wednesday's practice sessions at Indian Wells have since been removed by the WTA, but the footage had already been shared on social media.

It is understood the microphones were only intended to capture the sounds of rallies and not any conversations on court, and there will be no audio on future videos.

"The WTA takes full responsibility for failing to inform our players and their teams that microphones, in place to give fans a livestream of the players' practice, were active on the courts at the WTA Finals," a statement read.

"We sincerely apologise for failing to meet our responsibility to ensure players and coaches were properly informed."

Pegula, who is a member of the WTA players' council, also praised Andreeva, saying the world number three is "wonderful" and "smart".

The season-ending WTA Finals, being held at Indian Wells for the first time, run until 15 November.

Pegula's representative and the WTA have been approached for comment.

In a separate incident, world number one Elena Rybakina appeared to have an angry exchange with her coach before a practice session with Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova.

Some of the audio is unclear, but Pegula can be heard describing how Andreeva and Martinez complained throughout the session, even though Andreeva won every game.

Pegula: "Conchita's always been very nice to me, but I've lost a little respect for her because I'm like, this girl - I think she's a nice girl - she's just a diva. She needs to be humbled. She needs to be [inaudible] putting her in her place; [inaudible] stand up to her."

Spaniard Martinez - the 1994 Wimbledon champion - began working with Andreeva in April 2024. Andreeva reached the Wimbledon quarter-finals last year and claimed her first Grand Slam title at Roland Garros in June.

Pegula: "Conchita pokes her and eggs on her behaviour."

Knowles: "She needs somebody to put her in her place. Once she gets that, I think she'll be really good. I mean, she's already really good. Look how she moves."

Pegula: "She moves like a cat. She's wonderful. She's got the perfect serve. She's smart. She anticipates well."

Pegula, who has not won a Grand Slam, then compared Andreeva to world number four Coco Gauff. The American was also 19 when she won her first Grand Slam. Now 22, she has won two majors.

Pegula: "It's so funny how you see her and then you see Coco's mentality. If she had Coco's mentality, she'd be better than her."

Pegula: "The serve, everything, all-around, and she moves just as good. But like mentally, she's..."

Pegula and Andreeva are in different groups at the WTA Finals but could meet in the semi-finals or final.

Pegula's group opponents are Gauff, Rybakina and Noskova, and the latter pair's practice session at Indian Wells was also live-streamed.

Australian and US Open champion Rybakina appears to remonstrate with coach Stefano Vukov as they walk to the net, saying: "Stay here. I'm talking to you. Can you stand here?"

They shared a few more words, which are inaudible, before going to the other side of the court together to greet Noskova and her team.

Vukov was suspended by the WTA in February 2025 following an independent investigation into his behaviour towards Kazakhstan's Rybakina. He returned to her team that August.

Pegula was among the players to complain about additional behind-the-scenes cameras at the Australian Open in January.

The semi-finalist described the filming as an "invasion of privacy" that needs to be "cut back".

"You just feel like you're under a microscope constantly," she said.

title: Carlos Alcaraz through to Rolex Paris Masters quarter-finals after Matteo Berrettini withdraws injured
article_text:
Carlos Alcaraz made it through to the quarter-finals at the Rolex Paris Masters without taking to the court after his scheduled opponent Matteo Berrettini withdrew from their third-round match.

The pair had been due to play on Thursday evening in the French capital but Berrettini has suffered another injury setback, pulling out due to pain in his arm.

Alcaraz, who is chasing his fifth tour-level trophy of the season in the French capital, will face home favourite Arthur Fils or Taylor Fritz in the last eight at the ATP Masters 1000 event.

The Spaniard will be bidding to reach the semi-finals on the indoor hard courts of Paris for the first time in six appearances.

An official social media announcement from the tournament read: "Matteo Berrettini has to withdraw from the Rolex Paris Masters. Wishing you a speedy recovery Matteo. Carlos Alcaraz is qualified for the quarter-finals."

Berrettini posted his statement of his own in Italian on Instagram stories, which translated as: "Hi all, unfortunately the pain in my arm that I've had for a few days won't allow me to take the court tonight.

"In the next few days I will have all the necessary tests to better understand what this is. Thank you all for the support and affection you show me every day on and off the court. Mat."

Fils, who will take on Fritz in the night session, became the first French player to qualify for the ATP Finals since Gael Monfils in 2016 earlier this week.

Fritz is currently 11th in the Race To Turin and still has a chance to qualify, although the American knows he must defeat both Fils and Alcaraz to reach the semi-finals to keep his hopes alive.

Alcaraz holds a 39-5 record for the season so far and has already qualified for the ATP Finals in Turin later this month having won four titles this year - Australian Open, Qatar Open, Japan Open and last week's Vienna Open.

title: ‘I’m talking to you!’ – Elena Rybakina’s anger caught on hot mic as WTA Finals chaos deepens

title: Mady Sow claims silver at Dakar 2026
article_text:
France's Mady Sow has secured the silver medal at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games after a hard-fought final against Riyan Malhan of the United Arab Emirates.

The reigning European Junior Champion, who also claimed bronze at the World Junior Championships earlier this year, came into the final looking to add another major title to his impressive 2026 season.

Despite leading for long periods of both games, the Frenchman eventually fell 17-21, 18-21.

In the opening game, Sow made a strong start and built an 11-7 lead. However, Malhan fought his way back into the contest and took the first game 21-17.

The second game followed a similar pattern, with Sow once again taking the lead and holding an 18-16 advantage late in the game. Unfortunately for the Frenchman, Malhan won five consecutive points to seal the victory and claim the gold medal.

Despite the defeat, it has been an impressive year for Sow. With a European Junior Championships gold medal, a World Junior Championships bronze medal and now a Youth Olympic Games silver medal, the Frenchman has added another major achievement to his Junior career.

A huge congratulations to Mady Sow on bringing home silver for France and Europe!

title: TCEMG suspends R$ 32 million sponsorship from Minas Gerais state-owned companies to football clubs
article_text:
TCEMG suspends R$ 32 million sponsorship from Minas Gerais state-owned companies to football clubs.

The Court of Auditors of the State of Minas Gerais (TCEMG) has suspended, in a precautionary decision, the sports sponsorship contracts worth R$ 32 million planned for 2027 between Minas Gerais state-owned companies and the clubs Cruzeiro, Atlético-MG and América-MG. The measure, signed this Tuesday (November 3rd) by acting councilor Licurgo Mourão, prevents the formalization of new agreements and orders the suspension of payments if contracts have already been signed.

The decision responds to Representation 1.220.989, presented by Senator and Governor-elect Cleitinho Azevedo (Republicans). In his statements, Cleitinho classified the sponsorship as "electioneering" and questioned the priority of the measure given the state's financial difficulties. "I cannot accept, as governor, taking more than R$ 30 million from Cemig and Codemig and putting it now into a football team. I will repeat again: everyone knows the love I have for football. But we have other priorities," declared the governor-elect.

The suspension was motivated by a series of irregularities identified by the rapporteur. No technical studies were presented to prove the institutional return on investment for the state-owned companies from the sponsorships, and the criteria used to define the amounts lack objectivity. Councilor Mourão stated that the initiative was announced by the state government as a way to compensate clubs for financial losses resulting from the ban on sports betting in Brazil, which raises doubts about the purpose of the public expenditure.

In this context, the contract values would have been calculated based on the needs of the beneficiary clubs, and not on the strategic interests of Cemig and Codemig, the state-owned sponsoring companies. The legislation requires the logic to be reversed: sponsorship must serve the business interests of the public entity, not the financial stability of the beneficiary.

The decision also points to the lack of information regarding feasibility studies, exposure of the state-owned companies' brands, and justification for the selection of the clubs involved. The fact that the contracts were announced in an election year adds another layer of scrutiny, given the legislation that imposes limits on advertising and sponsorship spending during that period.

Tension during the government transition.

This episode is part of a context of friction between the current government, led by Mateus Simões (PSD), and the transition team of Cleitinho Azevedo. The governor-elect had already expressed concerns about a projected deficit of R$ 10,5 billion for 2027 and about decisions by the current administration that, in his assessment, could compromise the state finances he will inherit in January.

“We are going through a transition, we are seeing the government itself saying that from January there may be money to pay the civil servants. We are going through a transition here and also seeing that there is a lack of school meals,” declared Cleitinho, indicating that sponsoring the clubs contradicts the priorities he intends to adopt in his administration.

Provisional decision, with merit review pending.

The suspension is temporary. The objective is to prevent the transfer of public funds while the court analyzes the legality, legitimacy, and cost-effectiveness of the agreements. The analysis of the merits of the Representation has not yet been concluded by the TCEMG (Court of Accounts of Minas Gerais).

The measure is already in effect and will be submitted to a referendum by the other council members at the next session of the First Chamber of the TCEMG (Court of Accounts of Minas Gerais), scheduled for next week. The outcome of this referendum will determine whether the suspension remains in place while the process is underway, but the central issue, which involves the use of state-owned companies to absorb losses in the football sector after the end of betting, remains unanswered until the merits of the case are judged.

title: Vunipola set for Tonga debut after completing switch from England
article_text:
Former England youth international Manu Vunipola has officially switched international allegiance to Tonga after being named in their squad for this weekend's Nations Cup match against Romania.

The fly-half's selection on the bench confirms his decision to represent Tonga, with the Pacific Islanders looking to build towards the 2027 Rugby World Cup in Australia.

Vunipola is the cousin of former England internationals Billy and Mako Vunipola, who remain eligible to switch allegiance to Tonga but have yet to make a decision on their international futures.

Mako has previously revealed his hopes of joining Tonga's coaching staff for the 2027 World Cup, although he acknowledges he is unlikely to still be playing by the time the tournament comes around.

Billy, meanwhile, has expressed reservations about making the switch, insisting he does not want to take a squad place away from a younger Tongan player.

World Rugby's three-year stand-down rule means Billy could still change his international allegiance, but his comments suggest a move is unlikely at this stage.

Manu Vunipola is a fly-half who was born in Auckland, New Zealand, but raised in Somerset, England.

He is the son of former Tonga international Elisi Vunipola and nephew of former Tonga internationals Fe'ao and Manu Vunipola.

His father, Elisi, featured at the 1995 and 1999 Rugby World Cups and was playing for Bay of Plenty on New Zealand's northern coast when Manu was born.

Vunipola came through the England age-grade system, representing the under-18s before making nine appearances for England under-20s.

He made his senior debut for Saracens in 2019 and became a regular contributor, scoring 17 points against both Ospreys and Sale Sharks in 2020.

The fly-half left Saracens to join Japan's Honda Heat in 2024.

He featured in eight matches at fly-half during last season's Japan Rugby League One campaign, although Honda Heat won just two of those fixtures.

Tonga face Romania in Bucharest tomorrow as they continue their preparations for the 2027 Rugby World Cup.

The Pacific Islanders will be looking to improve on their summer campaign, which saw them beat Zimbabwe but suffer defeats against Spain and Portugal.

With the World Cup fast approaching, Tonga are hoping to build momentum and establish their squad ahead of next year's tournament.

They have been drawn alongside England, Wales and Zimbabwe, meaning Vunipola could face the country he represented at youth level.

His international switch provides Tonga with another option at fly-half as they look to make an impact on the biggest stage in 2027.

title: WRU agree deal with rival nations as catastrophic relegation fears appear over
article_text:
A new deal has been agreed that will see Wales and nine other major rugby nations pool their commercial rights in a move that furthers their collective financial dominance of the sport and seemingly staves off any threat of relegation from the Nations Championship.

The teams from the Six Nations will join forces with the SANZAAR sides - South Africa, New Zealand, Australia and Argentina - in creating a new company to run the Nations Championship. It has been provisionally called F10, after the 10 founding unions; England, France, Scotland, Wales, Ireland, Italy, South Africa, New Zealand, Australia and Argentina.

The decision was made in a meeting in Sydney two weeks ago, with a dedicated chief executive to be appointed in order to focus on "commercial exploitation".

A right-management agency will also be created that will aggregate the commercial rights for a number of competitions.

“The Six Nations, Rugby Championship, Lions, Nations Championship, Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry will all be marketed and taken to market in a consolidated fashion,” Rugby Football Union chief executive Bill Sweeney told journalists this week.

That would not take place until the end of existing arrangements for the Six Nations rights with ITV, which run through to 2029.

“In effect, what we are creating is a commercial rights agency which sits underneath those 10 founding unions,” Sweeney said. “We think that will result in a much better and more efficient approach to market and obviously with the intention of increasing overall valuations and growing the commercial side of the game.”

Sweeney added that he believed pooling the commercial rights of the northern and southern hemisphere teams would "increase the revenue significantly" on broadcasting rights.

It is possible that the broadcast rights could be bundled together, leading to one broadcaster buying it up to become essentially the home of rugby.

However, there is a fear that this power grab will cast Tier Two nations further adrift.

Japan and Fiji are involved in the inaugural Nations Championship, but only as guest nations - receiving a participation fee rather than a piece of any central commercial income.

Promotion and relegation, which was intended for the Nations Championship when first backed by World Rugby's council three years ago, will seemingly not apply to the F10 nations.

That could come as a boost to Wales, given their standing towards the bottom of the northern hemisphere table - alongside Italy - at the moment. Such a demotion could have had a catastrophic financial and sporting impact for any relegated nation.

“There’s a review group that has been set up by World Rugby and is chaired by Brett Robinson,” Sweeney added. “They’re looking at how the aspect of promotion and relegation can be set up.

"The basic premise is still the same, how that comes into effect needs to be sorted out.”

Instead, either Japan or Fiji seem far likelier to make way for any new team in 2032.

With emerging nations playing in the secondary Nations Cup, it will continue to reduce the number of fixtures against Tier One nations - with World Cups the only realistic meeting place.

“I actually think this is better for the tier-two unions because you’ve got guaranteed fixtures, you’ve got more game time happening and you’ve got clarity about what you can play," said Sweeney.

The RFU CEO also confirmed that Qatar would not host the finals of the 2028 Nations Championship, due to unrest in the Middle East.

Both France and Spain have expressed an interest, while another finals weekend in London is another possibility.

title: Springboks star Manie Libbok confirms South Africa return
article_text:
Manie Libbok has officially confirmed his return to South Africa, with the Sharks announcing his signing ahead of next season.

The fly-half will leave the Hanazono Kintetsu Liners when his contract expires in Japan, bringing his spell overseas to an end and returning to Durban.

The move marks another major signing in South African rugby today, following the news that Malcolm Marx will join the Bulls.

Libbok began his professional career with the Bulls before joining the Sharks in 2020. He then moved to the Stormers in 2021, where he established himself as one of the leading fly-halves in South African rugby.

He played a key role in the Stormers' United Rugby Championship triumph, finishing as the competition's leading points scorer.

The 29-year-old made his Springboks debut in 2022 and featured prominently in their 2023 Rugby World Cup-winning campaign.

Known for his attacking creativity and kicking ability, Libbok moved to Japan's Hanazono Kintetsu Liners in 2025, continuing his career overseas.

However, his return to the Sharks presents an opportunity to make a fresh impact in Durban.

Having spent just one season with the club earlier in his career, Libbok now returns with considerably more experience and a World Cup winners' medal to his name.

With 34 Test caps for the Springboks and still only 29, he represents a significant addition to the Sharks' squad.

The Durban side currently sit fourth in the URC and boast a squad packed with Springboks, including Thomas du Toit, Andre Esterhuizen, Ox Nche, Eben Etzebeth and Ethan Hooker.

The arrival of Libbok at fly-half could provide the attacking spark needed to turn the Sharks into serious title contenders next season.

"For this next chapter of my career, there is no club I would rather be joining than the Sharks,” he said in a club statement.

“This is an iconic club with a proud history, there’s real excitement about the future, and I want to be part of what’s being built here.

"When I chatted with JP and heard his vision for the team, I knew straight away that there’s something special developing here, and I want to be part of it.

"You can feel the new energy and the culture building, and this is a club that isn’t afraid to do things differently. I’m all in.

“I’ve had a taste of Durban before, so coming back at this stage of my career with experience behind me, as the club starts a new era, means a lot to me.

"I can’t wait to pull on the black and white jersey, work with coaches and my teammates, and give everything I’ve got for the badge and our supporters.”

title: Malcolm Marx confirms next club as Springboks star ends transfer speculation
article_text:
Reigning World Rugby Player of the Year Malcolm Marx has officially confirmed his next club after announcing his departure from Japan.

The 32-year-old Springboks hooker will leave Kubota Spears at the end of the 2026-27 Japan Rugby League One season to join the Bulls.

Marx had been linked with several South African clubs in recent months, with the Sharks initially emerging as potential suitors as they prepare for the departure of Bongi Mbonambi.

However, the Bulls have now secured his signature, reuniting him with head coach Johan Ackermann, who originally signed and developed the hooker during their time together at the Lions.

The double World Cup winner's departure from Kubota Spears was announced by the Japanese club last week, with the Bulls now confirming his return to South Africa.

Marx will follow former Shizuoka Blue Revs captain Kwagga Smith in making the move from Japan Rugby League One to the Pretoria-based club.

“I am incredibly grateful for the opportunity to join such a historic and respected club as the Bulls next season,” said Marx in a statement.

WXV Global Series 2026 review: France
article_text:
Technical shortcomings and tactical naivety. That’s what cost France in New Zealand. That’s what has cost a rebuilding France since the beginning of 2026 according to François Ratier, as his first year as head coach of Les Bleues slows to a halt.

Les Bleues record book for 2026 reads 11 matches played, 296 points scored and 299 conceded, with six wins – against Italy, Ireland, Scotland, Wales, Australia and Canada – and five defeats, including four in as many matches against New Zealand, and another one to England.

Mixed with work-ons is probably the fairest assessment of 2026 for France. Just like 2025. And 2024. And every year back to their last title, the 2018 Women’s Six Nations. A few moments of brilliance – the win over Canada in La Rochelle was one; Pauline Bourdon Sansus’ officially recognised Try of the Year against England another; Pauline Barrat’s thoroughly impressive early international outings before another serious knee injury – but rather more near-misses, might-have-beens, and frustrations.

The three-defeat New Zealand leg of France’s WXV Global Series campaign shifted the pointer heavily towards the frustration side of the dial. Ratier recognised as much.

“[They were] three different matches,” he told French sports daily L’Equipe. “The first [an 81-12 defeat] was obviously a heavy blow, but we got over it.

“In the second [31-12], we saw a fightback, a real realisation of what we’re capable of, with some interesting strategic elements starting to fall into place. And the third [36-7] was more frustrating because we had chances again.

“We have this tendency to shoot ourselves in the foot through a lack of tactical and strategic leadership.”

There’s no denying they stared Black Ferns squarely in the eye in Lyon in their opening WXV Global Series outing, and did so again for an hour in the second match in New Zealand. But, there’s also no denying they fell apart late-on in Whangarei, shipping three tries in the final 15 minutes. And they were never in the hunt after failing to score early on in Christchurch.

This remains the never-ending story for Les Bleues. Look to the hour-mark of that second match in New Zealand, when France, 14-12 down, launched repeated assaults on the Black Ferns’ line only – when they did finally cross – to be held up. Or the very early exchanges of the final game, when the same thing happened.

No one is about to reductively suggest either result would have been different had those tries been scored, merely that the shape of the game that followed would have been different.

“As coaches, we bear some of the blame for the fact that we were unable to close out this sort of match,” Ratier admitted. “But the players also need to take responsibility.”

It seems they are. Fly-half Carla Arbez, who succeeded Joanna Grisez as the recipient of Midi Olympique’s Golden ‘Oscar’ for 2026, told the newspaper: “We didn’t really know how to approach the girls as they left the pitch [after the 81-12 loss in Hamilton], or how to handle the video debrief…

“But the staff really did a great job. They didn’t give us a dressing-down. Instead, they went back to basics and tried to help us with the strategic and tactical aspects, to understand where we had gone wrong and how to avoid going wrong in those moments. I think we did that well in the second match.”

Which made the third Test performance in Christchurch that much worse. “We’re making matches harder for ourselves,” Arbez admitted, “with our inefficiency in the scoring zone. If we scored every time we entered our opponents’ 22… things wouldn’t be the same for them mentally, or for us.”

Scoring every time is an impossible dream for even the maddest attack coaches, but the image Arbez paints is clear. France’s inability to score, their panic in the red zone – and the inevitable offload too far that it causes – is a weak point opponents will revel in. She knows it, the staff know it. It can be corrected.

But it takes time. “There’s still a lot of work to do for the Six Nations,” Arbez said, “and for the years to come.”

The ‘work’ to which Arbez refers goes right back to the basics. As Ratier told L’Equipe: “We identified [a] technical divide as soon as we arrived. That’s why we maintain basic skills like passing in training. However, you don’t do the most passing in training with the national team. There are the youth teams, the academies, the clubs…

“I’ve been saying the same thing since January – we lack the basic high-pressure skills we encounter in international matches.”

The nature of international selection – the squad isn’t due to gather again until next year – means that fundamental rugby skills have to be in the wheelhouse of the clubs and the players.

“This skills gap isn’t new,” Ratier said. “There are areas of training that are less fun to work on, like repeating technical skills. We don’t focus on that as much in France – but we have to because the skills gap could widen even further.”

France had taken a relatively inexperienced squad to New Zealand for the October tests. But Ratier wasn’t about to hide behind that.

“This isn’t a question of inexperience,” he said after that third and final defeat on tour. “If we look at our players at nine [captain, Alexandra Chambon], 10 [Arbez] and 15 [Émilie Boulard], they’re not players with just two caps. We’ll be having these discussions with the squad during the debrief.

title: 'One of America's great sports cities': Buffalo bids for MLR franchise
article_text:
Expansion is once again on the horizon for Major League Rugby. After a tumultuous 2025 offseason reduced the United States’ men’s professional league by half, MLR and a potential Buffalo ownership group have taken the first steps to establish a professional rugby club in Western New York by the 2028 season.

The prospective club is the Buffalo Thunderbolts Rugby Club, which was registered as a legal business entity in New York State on October 30, 2026. The project is being led by film producer Joe DiPasquale and former Miami Sharks CEO Mark Winokur.

The Thunderbolts — a name inspired by the World War II plane manufactured at the Curtiss aviation factories in Buffalo — also have the support of Buffalo Mayor Sean Ryan and New York State Assemblyman Bill Conrad. Conversations are underway to secure a stadium, and the ownership group is working to acquire further investment and sponsorship agreements.

“Buffalo is one of America’s great sports cities, and we would be excited to welcome Major League Rugby to our community,” Mayor Sean Ryan said. “I’m proud to support Joe DiPasquale and Mark Winokur’s efforts to bring an expansion team to Buffalo. This is an opportunity to build on our city’s proud sports tradition, introduce more people to rugby, and give our fans another team to rally behind.”

The letter of intent (LOI) signed by both parties is the first of three major steps in MLR’s expansion process. In the coming months, the Buffalo group must finalize its ownership group, provide proof of capitalization, demonstrate its expected fan engagement process, and show its preliminary business opportunity plans.

The league will determine whether those plans are acceptable by the end of April. If all goes well, the Thunderbolts and MLR will sign an exclusive negotiation agreement, giving the Buffalo group the rights to that territory (Western New York) for a specific period of time. After that, the Thunderbolts will submit a final bid to secure a franchise agreement.

Major League Rugby Co-President Alexander Magleby told RugbyPass that MLR hopes to announce two new franchises after the 2027 championship game. The league’s stated goal is to have eight teams going into the 2028 season and twelve by the time the 2031 Rugby World Cup in the US rolls around.

The LOI does not guarantee Buffalo will end up with an MLR franchise, but it is a major step in the right direction. It signals that both parties are willing to make their discussions public, which, of course, enables the Thunderbolts to appeal for public and private support.

Magleby said the league is “in discussion right now with 17 different [ownership] groups,” with some still going through the initial due diligence phase and others, like Buffalo, prepared to sign an LOI.

Given the various interested ownership groups, there will be plenty of competition for the two franchise expansion slots. The most competitive bids will ultimately be the winners, and that will depend on the economic and sporting value each bidder can bring to American rugby.

Still, both parties are excited about the prospect of a professional franchise coming to Western New York; after all, Buffalo is a mid-market city with a 60-year rugby union tradition and close ties to several universities and Toronto, Canada’s biggest metropolitan area.

DiPasquale, who describes himself as “a huge rugby fan,” acknowledges that there has been a gap in the regional market since Rugby United New York, Toronto Wolfpack, and the Arrows all folded. Appealing to a market that provides fervent support to its sports teams and recently introduced rugby into its middle school sports offerings makes perfect sense to DiPasquale.

“Number one is the rugby culture here,” said DiPasquale when asked about bringing a rugby team to Buffalo. “It’s amazing the support we’ve gotten across the board from the mayor, Assemblyman Conrad, and sponsors. That component alone makes this market wonderfully perfect for this.”

The Major League Rugby season takes place between the last weekend of March and late June, avoiding the NFL season completely and overlapping slightly with the NHL postseason. As DiPasquale puts it, “The rugby season falls perfectly. Unless the [Buffalo] Sabres make the playoffs, there’s nothing going on.”

“Rugby has been an instrumental part of my life since I was a very young man, when I played for SUNY Fredonia, and I later founded the Kenmore Rugby Club and coached kids in the sport for many years,” said New York State Assemblyman Bill Conrad, 140th District. “I love the game and what it did for my personal growth, my physical fitness and self-discipline, and my understanding of teamwork and leadership. I embrace any opportunity to introduce more of the world to the sport, and Buffalo offers an already strong base of rugby players, boosters, and fans. I couldn’t agree more that it’s a logical locale for an MLR expansion!”

While the goal is to solidify the franchise and draw in supporters from Western New York and Ontario, the prospective ownership group is realistic about their short-term ambitions. They are in “very serious meetings” for a venue that could hold up to 10,000 fans, although DiPasquale said they will be shooting for 3,000 to 5,000 fans to start.

“I believe that we (Buffalo) are also a leader in sports in the US,” said DiPasquale. “Buffalo could have an exponential impact on the league,” he added before likening the location and the new franchise to the historically great NFL city and franchise of Green Bay.

title: Italy turn to 142kg Bath giant amid injury crisis for Boks
article_text:
Italy have named a heavily reshuffled side to face South Africa in Turin on Saturday, with Gonzalo Quesada forced to contend with a lengthy injury list for the Nations Championship clash.

Captain Michele Lamaro, Sebastian Negri, Marco Riccioni, Andrea Zambonin and Tommaso Menoncello are among a host of players unavailable for the meeting with the world champions.

Samuele Locatelli will make his Test debut at openside, joining Lorenzo Cannone and Alessandro Ortombina in the back-row, while Giacomo Nicotera captains the side for only the second time.

There is considerable size on the bench, where 142kg Bath forward Enoch Opoku-Gyamfi is included. The 20-year-old’s only previous Test appearance came against Chile last year, and he now has another chance to impress against the Springboks.

Paolo Garbisi and Alessandro Fusco form the half-back pairing, with Leonardo Marin and Paolo Odogwu in midfield. The centres will be filling in for the absent Juan Ignacio Brex and Tommaso Menoncello, who will be sorely missed in northern Italy. Monty Ioane will win his 50th cap on the left wing, with Ange Capuozzo on the right and Mirko Belloni at full-back.

Ferrari and Allan are the only two survivors in the matchday squad from Italy’s famous victory over South Africa in Florence in 2016.

Saturday’s fixture will be the 20th meeting between the nations and the second in succession staged in Turin. Italy then face Argentina in Genoa and Fiji in Udine before travelling to Twickenham’s Allianz Stadium for the Nations Championship Finals Weekend later this month.
